scope: Follow-up of the 200 incomplete profile claims

reviews.claimText: Associated with tall forest in the Central Nature Reserves and connected wooded spaces. A quiet, hidden animal may be present even when visitors do not notice it.
reviews.note: Flora & Fauna Web names the central reserves and adjacent parkland. BiodiversitySG explains tall-forest use, camouflage and concealed daytime rest.

reviews.claimText: Do not handle a bat or disturb a roost. Observe from a distance and seek professional help for an injured animal.
reviews.note: AVS gives non-handling and professional rescue advice. The roost and fruit dependence supports the qualitative habitat-loss inference, not a measured decline.

reviews.claimText: Loss of roosts and fruiting vegetation can remove shelter and food.
reviews.note: AVS gives non-handling and professional rescue advice. The roost and fruit dependence supports the qualitative habitat-loss inference, not a measured decline.

reviews.claimText: An omnivore. Regional research records fruit and other plant material, some animal food and mushrooms; the proportions in Singapore have not been measured here.
reviews.note: The 2026 paper documents mushroom feeding in Indonesia in 2020 and reviews other foods. It explicitly states that spore dispersal remains unproven.

reviews.claimText: Consumes material from several parts of the forest food web. Mushroom eating is documented, but effective fungal-spore dispersal by this species remains a research question.
reviews.note: The 2026 paper documents mushroom feeding in Indonesia in 2020 and reviews other foods. It explicitly states that spore dispersal remains unproven.

reviews.claimText: Lays eggs. Breeding has been achieved in conservation collections; no Singapore nesting month or clutch-size claim is made here.
reviews.note: The zoo account and Durrell breeding report document eggs and captive breeding. Captive timing is not a Singapore nesting calendar.

reviews.claimText: Common in buildings and nearby wooded areas. It is listed in Singapore’s national reptile assessment as Least Concern.
reviews.note: The Jurong Lake Gardens gecko section confirms buildings and nearby forests. RDB3 separately supplies the national Least Concern category.

reviews.claimText: A native resident of wooded areas and some neighbourhoods. The name Sumatran palm civet follows NParks’ current species table.
reviews.note: BiodiversitySG uses Paradoxurus musangus and describes forests and gardens. AVS adds neighbourhood occurrence under the older name; RDB3 confirms native status.

reviews.claimText: Associated with patches of mature forest in the Central Nature Reserves. It is nationally Critically Endangered in RDB3; this guide avoids breeding-site directions.
reviews.note: The Singapore field paper confines occurrence to the central reserves. RDB3 replaces its historical national category with Critically Endangered.
